help.settings.workspace.title: Workspace profile
help.settings.workspace.what:
This card gives you a quick identity check for your current workspace.
Use it to confirm name, timezone, and your role before changing privacy, billing, or team settings.
help.settings.workspace.fields:
Workspace name: the active workspace you are editing.
Timezone: the reference timezone used by operational features.
Role badge: shows whether you currently have admin-level permissions.
help.settings.workspace.actions:
If the workspace or timezone looks wrong, switch workspace first.
If your role is not admin and you need privileged actions, ask an admin to grant access.
help.settings.workspace.tip: Always verify this card first when numbers or schedules look off; most confusion starts from the wrong workspace context.
help.settings.account.title: Account
help.settings.account.what:
This section shows the identity currently signed in to the dashboard.
It is useful for audits, support tickets, and API troubleshooting.
help.settings.account.fields:
Email: your active login.
ID: your internal user identifier used in logs and backend support.
help.settings.account.actions:
Use these values when support asks who executed an action.
If the account is not the one you expect, sign out and continue with the right user.
help.settings.account.tip: When reporting an issue, include your user ID; it speeds up debugging a lot.
help.settings.preferences.title: Preferences
help.settings.preferences.what:
This section controls your personal dashboard experience.
It does not change production data; it changes how the UI appears for you.
help.settings.preferences.fields:
Theme: dark, light, or system-following mode.
Language: interface locale used across the dashboard.
help.settings.preferences.actions:
Pick the language your team is most comfortable with.
Set theme to system if you want automatic day/night behavior.
help.settings.preferences.tip: After changing language, quickly scan key pages (Issues, Alerts, Settings) to ensure labels are clear for your workflow.
help.settings.replayPrivacy.title: Replay privacy
help.settings.replayPrivacy.what:
This policy masks sensitive values before replay data is stored.
Use it to reduce privacy risk while keeping enough context for debugging.
help.settings.replayPrivacy.fields:
Mask mode: full replaces secrets fully, partial keeps small parts for easier debugging.
Redact keys: field names to always mask (comma-separated).
Regex rules: patterns to detect and redact dynamic sensitive text.
Test input + masked preview: safe sandbox to validate your policy before saving.
help.settings.replayPrivacy.actions:
Start with Full mask in production, then move to Partial only if troubleshooting needs extra context.
Add common keys like password/token/cookie and your own domain-specific fields.
Paste a realistic sample payload in test input and verify preview output before saving.
help.settings.replayPrivacy.tip: Keep regex rules focused and tested; broad patterns can over-mask useful debugging data.
help.settings.dsar.title: GDPR / DSAR
help.settings.dsar.what:
Use this section to run privacy requests such as export or delete for data subjects.
It is designed for legal/compliance workflows and should be handled carefully.
help.settings.dsar.fields:
Type: export or delete.
Identifiers: email, user ID, and/or IP values used to locate records.
Requests table: status, timestamps, result, and available actions.
help.settings.dsar.actions:
Choose the right request type, enter reliable identifiers, then create the request.
Track progress in the table; run, inspect details, and download export when ready.
help.settings.dsar.tip: Submit the smallest precise identifier set possible to avoid accidental overreach.
help.alerts.ruleBuilder.title: Create alert rule
help.alerts.ruleBuilder.what:
This form turns an observed problem into an automated alert.
A good rule should notify the right team, at the right time, without noisy false alarms.
help.alerts.ruleBuilder.fields:
Name: readable rule name tied to a clear use-case.
Rule type + threshold: detection logic and trigger sensitivity.
Destinations: where notifications are delivered.
Enabled toggle: whether this rule starts active immediately.
help.alerts.ruleBuilder.actions:
Begin with a simple rule and one destination, then expand advanced settings only when needed.
Set thresholds using real incident history so alerts are actionable.
Enable the rule only after confirming destinations and scope are correct.
help.alerts.ruleBuilder.tip: Prefer fewer high-quality alerts over many weak alerts; signal quality beats alert quantity.
help.projects.catalog.title: Projects Catalog
help.projects.catalog.what: This page lists all services connected to Errnox. Use it to find the right project before any change.
help.projects.catalog.fields: Search finds projects by name/slug/platform. Status filter narrows active or disabled projects. Rows show platform, environment, and state.
help.projects.catalog.actions: Search first, open project details, then make changes like retention or keys.
help.projects.catalog.tip: Check platform and environment first to avoid triage mistakes.
help.projects.createProject.title: Create Project
help.projects.createProject.what: This modal creates a new service project in your workspace.
help.projects.createProject.fields: Name is team-friendly label. Platform helps defaults. Default environment tags new events.
help.projects.createProject.actions: Use a clear service name, pick the real platform, create, then finish setup in Project Settings.
help.projects.createProject.tip: Consistent naming saves time in alerts and ownership.
help.members.overview.title: Team Members
help.members.overview.what: Manage who has access and what each member can do.
help.members.overview.fields: Invite section sends access links. Pending list tracks unaccepted invites. Member cards show active roles.
help.members.overview.actions: Give least privilege, review pending invites, and update roles when responsibilities change.
help.members.overview.tip: Treat role changes like production changes: intentional and documented.
help.members.invite.title: Invite New Member
help.members.invite.what: Send a secure invitation to a teammate.
help.members.invite.fields: Email receives invitation. Role sets initial permissions. Invite link can be copied manually.
help.members.invite.actions: Enter correct work email, choose role carefully, send invite, then verify it appears in pending invites.
help.members.invite.tip: Start with lower access for sensitive workspaces.
help.members.pendingInvites.title: Pending Invitations
help.members.pendingInvites.what: Track invites that are sent but not accepted yet.
help.members.pendingInvites.fields: Each row shows email, role, expiry. Resend issues fresh token. Cancel revokes invitation.
help.members.pendingInvites.actions: Resend missed invites, cancel stale ones, and watch expirations for urgent onboarding.
help.members.pendingInvites.tip: Cleaning old invites improves security hygiene.
help.members.rolesMatrix.title: Role Matrix
help.members.rolesMatrix.what: Review available roles and exact permissions before assigning access.
help.members.rolesMatrix.fields: Role key identifies level. Permissions list shows capabilities.
help.members.rolesMatrix.actions: Validate permissions before admin-level access. Prefer least privilege by default.
help.members.rolesMatrix.tip: Clear role policy prevents over-access and bottlenecks.
help.destinations.management.title: Alert Destinations
help.destinations.management.what: Control where alerts are delivered: email, Telegram, Slack, or webhook.
help.destinations.management.fields: Destination cards show health and status. Actions include test, pause/resume, settings, and logs.
help.destinations.management.actions: Keep verified channels for critical projects and always run tests after important changes.
help.destinations.management.tip: Delivery quality matters more than alert quantity.
help.destinations.createDestination.what: Create a new notification channel using the provider tabs.
help.destinations.createDestination.fiel: Name labels channel. Provider fields define endpoint. Submit validates and saves.
help.destinations.createDestination.acti: Choose matching provider, enter production-ready endpoints, then send a test alert.
help.destinations.createDestination.tip: Use channel names that show team and purpose.
help.destinations.channelSettings.title: Channel Settings
help.destinations.channelSettings.what: Tune routing and noise behavior for one channel.
help.destinations.channelSettings.fields: Allowed projects set scope. Noise controls tune rate/duplicate suppression. Quiet and digest tune off-hours behavior.
help.destinations.channelSettings.action: Start balanced, adjust with real traffic, set timezone/quiet hours, then validate with tests.
help.destinations.deliveryLogs.title: Delivery Logs
help.destinations.deliveryLogs.what: Inspect recent delivery attempts for one destination.
help.destinations.deliveryLogs.fields: Status shows delivered/suppressed/failed. Attempts show retries. Error message shows failure reason.
help.destinations.deliveryLogs.actions: Focus recent failures, fix config/connectivity, then retest and confirm delivered.
help.destinations.deliveryLogs.tip: Recurring failures usually mean config drift.
help.projectSettings.overview.title: Project Settings Overview
help.projectSettings.overview.what: Control center for one project: profile, API key, and SDK setup.
help.projectSettings.overview.fields: Profile card manages identity and grouping. API key card manages key lifecycle. Snippets card helps setup.
help.projectSettings.overview.actions: Validate profile first, rotate keys carefully, and complete SDK wiring in service repo.
help.projectSettings.overview.tip: Wrong values here affect issues, alerts, and reports.
help.projectSettings.profile.title: Project Profile
help.projectSettings.profile.what: Define project metadata and event grouping behavior.
help.projectSettings.profile.fields: Name/platform/environment/status/retention control identity and data lifecycle. Grouping controls dedup behavior.
help.projectSettings.profile.actions: Keep values aligned with production runtime and verify grouping output after saving.
help.projectSettings.profile.tip: Tune grouping with real incidents, not guesses.
help.projectSettings.apiKey.title: Project API Key
help.projectSettings.apiKey.what: This key authenticates data ingestion into this project.
help.projectSettings.apiKey.fields: Current key is active credential. Copy helps secure transfer. Rotate replaces old key.
help.projectSettings.apiKey.actions: Store in secret manager, rotate during controlled rollout, and verify ingestion after rotation.
help.projectSettings.apiKey.tip: Treat key rotation like certificate rotation.
help.projectSettings.snippets.title: SDK Snippets
help.projectSettings.snippets.what: Get install and quick-start code based on platform.
help.projectSettings.snippets.fields: Install command sets package. Quick start initializes SDK. Docs link opens full guide.
help.projectSettings.snippets.actions: Copy snippet, adapt to your config, keep key in env vars, then test data flow.
help.projectSettings.snippets.tip: Start minimal, then add advanced instrumentation.
help.plansUsage.overview.title: Plans & Usage
help.plansUsage.overview.what: Review billing status, usage pressure, and upgrade risk.
help.plansUsage.overview.fields: Plan summary shows cycle/state. Usage cards show events/storage vs limits. Advisor shows upgrade risk and actions.
help.plansUsage.overview.actions: Check before high-traffic launches, review trends weekly, and plan upgrades proactively.
help.plansUsage.currentPlan.title: Current Plan
help.plansUsage.currentPlan.what: Quick snapshot of subscription state and billing window.
help.plansUsage.currentPlan.fields: Plan/status/cycle explain contract state. Period/renewal define timing. Retention defines data lifespan.
help.plansUsage.currentPlan.actions: Confirm cycle dates and retention policy before making capacity decisions.
help.plansUsage.currentPlan.tip: Retention mismatch is a common storage problem.
help.plansUsage.usage.title: Usage & Limits
help.plansUsage.usage.what: Track consumed events and storage against quota.
help.plansUsage.usage.fields: Used/limit/remaining values plus percentage bars show current pressure.
help.plansUsage.usage.actions: React early to near-limit signals and reduce noisy telemetry before hard limits.
help.plansUsage.usage.tip: Sudden spikes often come from instrumentation mistakes.
help.plansUsage.upgradeAdvisor.title: Upgrade Advisor
help.plansUsage.upgradeAdvisor.fields: Severity/score/confidence describe risk. Projections show expected usage. Actions show practical next steps.
help.plansUsage.upgradeAdvisor.actions: Read reasons, prioritize actions, and schedule upgrade quickly when confidence and severity are high.
help.plansUsage.upgradeAdvisor.tip: High-confidence warnings need action, not delay.
help.plansUsage.latestPayment.title: Latest Payment
help.plansUsage.latestPayment.what: Shows the most recent billing transaction details.
help.plansUsage.latestPayment.fields: Amount/currency, status/method, and exact payment timestamp.
help.plansUsage.latestPayment.actions: If payment failed, verify gateway/retry state and share details with finance/support.
help.plansUsage.latestPayment.tip: Payment time and usage spikes together help explain billing anomalies.
help.support.overview.title: Support center overview
help.support.overview.what: Use this page to triage ticket status, inspect conversation history, and create or reply to requests without leaving context.
help.support.overview.fields:
Status filter: narrows queue quickly.
Ticket list: current page of requests.
Ticket detail: selected conversation timeline.
Create form: new ticket submission area.
help.support.overview.actions:
Filter the queue by status first.
Open the target ticket and review latest messages.
Reply with clear next action and evidence.
Create a new ticket when issue is not already tracked.
help.support.overview.tip: Set priority based on business impact, not only technical severity, to keep response queues healthy.
help.support.ticketFilters.title: Ticket filters
help.support.ticketFilters.what: Filter controls reduce noise so operators can focus on open or pending conversations.
help.support.ticketFilters.fields:
All: full queue.
Open: waiting for action.
Pending: waiting for counterpart response.
Closed: resolved conversations.
help.support.ticketFilters.actions:
Select one status before reviewing list.
Reset to All when searching broadly across tickets.
help.support.ticketFilters.tip: Use Pending during follow-up windows to catch stalled tickets quickly.
help.support.ticketList.title: Ticket list panel
help.support.ticketList.what: Shows paged tickets with subject, status, priority, and last activity time to choose the right thread fast.
help.support.ticketList.fields:
Subject: short request headline.
Ticket ID: stable reference for sharing.
Status badge: current lifecycle state.
Priority badge: urgency level.
help.support.ticketList.actions:
Sort mentally by status and freshness.
Open the most impactful ticket first.
Use pagination for older tickets.
help.support.ticketList.tip: If labels feel dense, keep subject concise to improve scan speed for all languages.
help.support.ticketConversation.title: Conversation detail panel
help.support.ticketConversation.what: Displays full message thread and metadata so you can answer with context and clear ownership.
help.support.ticketConversation.fields:
Sender/recipient: who said what to whom.
Sent time: exact timeline anchor.
Internal note: operator-only context.
Message body: actionable details.
help.support.ticketConversation.actions:
Read latest message first.
Confirm owner and next step.
Reply with explicit timeline and expected outcome.
help.support.ticketConversation.tip: Keep one decision per reply to reduce misunderstandings in multi-language support threads.
help.support.createTicket.title: Create ticket form
help.support.createTicket.what: Use this form to open a new request with enough context for fast and accurate handling.
help.support.createTicket.fields:
Subject: feature + impact summary.
Priority: urgency based on user/business effect.
Message: reproduction steps and expected behavior.
Attachments: links to logs, screenshots, traces.
help.support.createTicket.actions:
Write a clear subject first.
Choose realistic priority.
Add structured message and evidence links.
Submit when required fields are complete.
help.support.createTicket.tip: Good initial context reduces back-and-forth and shortens mean time to resolution.
help.support.replyBox.title: Reply box
help.support.replyBox.what: Send follow-up answers on the selected ticket while preserving conversation chronology.
help.support.replyBox.fields:
Reply text: next action, timeline, blockers.
Send button: submits current draft.
help.support.replyBox.actions:
Keep replies short and concrete.
Mention what changed and what is expected next.
help.support.replyBox.tip: Include a verification step in each reply to make progress measurable.
help.apiKeys.overview.title: API keys center
help.apiKeys.overview.what: Manage project ingest keys, rotate credentials safely, and copy SDK snippets for quick integration.
help.apiKeys.overview.fields:
Project selector: active key scope.
Primary key card: current ingest key.
SDK guide: copy-paste setup snippets.
help.apiKeys.overview.actions:
Select project first.
Copy key or rotate if compromised.
Use SDK tab matching your stack.
help.apiKeys.overview.tip: After key rotation, update all producers immediately to avoid ingestion gaps.
help.apiKeys.projectList.title: Projects for key management
help.apiKeys.projectList.what: Lists projects so you can switch key context quickly and avoid editing the wrong project.
help.apiKeys.projectList.fields:
Project name: target service.
Platform tag: runtime family.
help.apiKeys.projectList.actions:
Pick the project before copying or rotating key.
Confirm environment in snippets afterwards.
help.apiKeys.projectList.tip: Use consistent project naming to reduce accidental key sharing.
help.apiKeys.primaryKey.title: Primary API key
help.apiKeys.primaryKey.what: Current project key used by SDKs and backend ingestion clients.
help.apiKeys.primaryKey.fields:
Key value: sensitive credential.
Rotate action: revokes old key and issues new one.
Copy action: puts key in clipboard.
help.apiKeys.primaryKey.actions:
Rotate only with rollout plan.
Update secret stores and deployments right after rotation.
help.apiKeys.primaryKey.tip: Treat copied keys as secrets and avoid sharing them in tickets or chat.
help.apiKeys.sdkGuide.title: SDK quick-start guide
help.apiKeys.sdkGuide.what: Framework tabs provide install command and starter snippet for each supported language.
help.apiKeys.sdkGuide.fields:
Install command: dependency setup.
Init snippet: apiKey + environment bootstrap.
Docs link: full integration reference.
help.apiKeys.sdkGuide.actions:
Select your stack tab.
Copy snippet and set real environment value.
Validate by sending a test event.
help.apiKeys.sdkGuide.tip: Keep environment names identical across dashboard and SDK initialization.
help.projectSettingsHub.overview.title: Project settings hub
help.projectSettingsHub.overview.what: Central table to search projects, inspect core settings, and jump to detailed configuration quickly.
help.projectSettingsHub.overview.fields:
Search: filter by name/platform.
Status chips: active/disabled scope.
Table rows: project metadata and actions.
help.projectSettingsHub.overview.actions:
Filter list first.
Open project settings for deep edits.
Use quick actions for key access and copy.
help.projectSettingsHub.overview.tip: Review status and environment before changing settings to avoid wrong-project edits.
Shows a ready-to-copy SDK snippet using selected project key and default environment.

Install command: minimal dependency step.
Snippet block: project-bound initialization template.

Validate project selection first.
Copy snippet and replace placeholders in your codebase.
Run a smoke event after deployment to confirm new settings are applied.
help.general.pageHeader.title: Page header guidance
help.general.pageHeader.what: This header explains the page purpose and gives access to key actions for the current workflow.
help.general.pageHeader.fields:
Title: main context of the page.
Description: short summary of the outcome.
Action bar: fast operations for this page.
help.general.pageHeader.actions:
Read title/description before changes.
Use action buttons only after verifying selected project/workspace.
help.general.pageHeader.tip: If outputs look wrong, validate workspace, project, and time range first.
help.general.widgetCard.title: Section card guidance
help.general.widgetCard.what: Each card groups a single task area such as filters, charts, tables, or settings.
help.general.widgetCard.fields:
Card title: section identity.
Subtitle: usage intent.
Body: controls and outputs related to one task.
help.general.widgetCard.actions:
Complete card inputs from top to bottom.
Review chart/table output in the same card before moving on.
help.general.widgetCard.tip: Treat each card as one unit of work to avoid mixing unrelated changes.
help.general.routeTabs.title: Page tabs
help.general.routeTabs.what: Tabs switch between related pages in the same domain without losing navigation context.
help.general.routeTabs.fields:
Active tab: current page.
Other tabs: sibling pages in the same workflow.
help.general.routeTabs.actions: Use tabs for domain navigation first, then use sidebar for moving to another domain.
help.general.routeTabs.tip: If you are unsure where to continue, choose the active domain tab before changing filters.
help.general.fallback.title: Section info
help.general.fallback.what: This section contains important controls for the current page workflow.
help.general.fallback.fields:
Review labels and placeholders in this section.
Inputs affect table and chart outputs.
help.general.fallback.actions:
Fill required fields first.
Apply filters in small steps and verify results.
help.general.fallback.tip: Use the page guide button for full step-by-step instructions.
help.general.filters.title: Filters and inputs
help.general.filters.what: This area controls search, filter, and query scope for charts and tables on the page.
help.general.filters.fields:
